utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning. Madam Registrar, can you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All the accused are here. From the Defence teams I notice the absence of Mr. Lazarevic, Mr. Haynes. That's about it, I think. Prosecution is the same team, Mr. McCloskey, and Ms. Janisiewicz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand that there is some preliminary. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted to say that with respect to the matter we discussed yesterday, the documents that should be disclosed to us under Rule 70 are indeed the diary of the -- of Witness 14 and other documents that are very relevant in terms of the testimony of General Schmidt. Second thing, yesterday we received an interview of the witness currently before us. I would therefore ask the Chamber to allow me to cross-examine the witness for a further 10 minutes based on the interview I received yesterday. Of course at the moment I can't tell you if I really need the entire 10 minutes because my colleagues might cover all these issues, but nonetheless, I'd like to ask for 10 extra minutes to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What interview -- thank you, Madam Fauveau. What interview is Madam Fauveau referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We, on request of the Nikolic team, found a transcript and a video of an interview with the witness that had been provided to the Defence in the form of a signed statement, and so we were not aware until we looked in a place that -- you know how the system works, but we found a misfiled videotape of something that had been done by another team, a signed statement of the interview. So they had a signed statement of the interview but then in addition to that we found a video and a transcript. So they need -- Ms. Fauveau is looking at that video and transcript to see if there's anything new or different than the signed statement. So I have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. This is an issue that came about before last night and we have not addressed the Trial Chamber at this time, but we will do so after the end of my cross-examination. We feel that the situation is much more complex than what has been described by my colleague, but we don't want to address it at this time because it's not only one tape that is missing, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So we will address the Trial Chamber in this respect after the end of my cross-examination. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. The pleasure is yet to come. We've taken note of what you have stated. You still have to come back to us on the Rule 70 issues, still unresolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. No news on that. We're still talking with New York and trying to get them had to speed up. So that's not an issue. We have been able -- or can we be in closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 29th day of October, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.42 p.m.,
